reviews.one_line_contribution: It treats the four metric families used to develop agent experience memories (episode recall/MRR, LLM-judge item quality, admission-gate F1, memory reward-model scores) as clinical-trial surrogate endpoints and measures their validity for execution success directly - via attenuation-corrected rank correlation, Freedman's proportion explained, and selection regret across a pre-registered 20-configuration family on ALFWorld/WebShop - then offers a cheap prefix-agreement probe as a validated replacement.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, splitting the proposal in half. (a) On the destructive half, arXiv:2510.21440 'Redefining Retrieval Evaluation in the Era of LLMs' (verified via s2cli, S2+HF channel) and arXiv:2512.20854 'How important is Recall for Measuring Retrieval Quality?' (same channel) already establish, on RAG, that recall-family metrics correlate poorly with end-to-end answer accuracy and that distractor cost must enter the metric; arXiv:2606.23937 (verified, cited by the proposal) does the tool-use-policy version; arXiv:2607.00725 (verified - note the real title is 'Recall Is Not Enough: A Reader-Context Diagnostic for Budget-Constrained RAG', not 'What Survives Into Context' as the proposal states) does the multi-hop version; and arXiv:2608.00017 (verified) already shows LLM self-grading is blind to wrong episodes in agent memory. Each surrogate's individual invalidity is therefore one short hop from published work; what is left unclaimed is the joint comparison plus the Prentice/Freedman formalism, which my searches did not find anywhere in the LLM literature. (b) On the constructive half, arXiv:2609.02783 'EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction' (verified on S2, dated 2026-09-02, five days before this proposal) trains classifiers over behavioral, textual and reference-solution features to predict agent outcomes from a run prefix and halt early - that is the proposed prefix-agreement probe's core idea, with a reference-solution feature standing in for the 'verified success trajectory'. arXiv:2607.02032 (PACE, verified) and arXiv:2605.06455 (PrefixGuard, verified) occupy adjacent ground. The proposal's P5 is therefore not a new construct; at best it is a new application of a five-day-old published one, and the proposal shows no awareness of it.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline number is a rank correlation over n=20 configurations, used to ACCEPT a null ('corrected tau below 0.5', 'below 0.3'), with an attenuation correction whose denominator is itself estimated from 2 seeds. At n=20 the sampling CI on Kendall tau is roughly +/-0.3, so the design cannot separate tau=0.45 from tau=0.75, and a two-level bootstrap over 20 units will not rescue it. Worse, the correction makes the predictions nearly self-fulfilling in the authors' preferred direction: if endpoint test-retest reliability comes in at ~0.4 (entirely plausible given this program's own pilot, where re-scoring the same candidate moved the headline metric by 0.05-0.14 and a null replicate matched the best real treatment), then 'corrected tau < 0.5' only requires raw tau < 0.32, which is close to guaranteed by noise alone. The confound this cannot exclude is the obvious one: a low tau because the ENDPOINT barely varies across the family, not because the surrogates are invalid. The plan has no pre-registered positive control establishing that the true across-configuration endpoint spread is large relative to the ~3-point MDE, and P4 ('the surrogate-selected configuration is indistinguishable from memoryless') is nearly trivially satisfied in a setting where this program has already measured memory to be null-to-harmful. A second, independent version of the same objection: the estimand is a property of the configuration family, not of the surrogates, and the family is partly engineered to produce the result - the adversarial-nearest-wrong arm is constructed to be high-judge-score and task-wrong, so P2 is a demonstration by construction rather than a measurement of how judges behave on configurations anyone deploys. 'Top-half correlation' does not define the population being sampled.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Decouple the two cost axes: surrogates are cheap, the endpoint is not, so expand the confirmatory family to 50-60 configurations sampled from a defined population (e.g. the configurations instantiated in ReMe/MemRL/A-MAC/ExpeL and their neighbourhoods) and cut to 300 tasks x 3 seeds if needed; report the correlation both on the full family and on the 'deployable' subfamily with the adversarial and random arms excluded, and pre-register the latter as the confirmatory estimand since that is the one that speaks to practice. (2) Replace null-acceptance with equivalence testing: pre-register a one-sided TOST-style bound against tau=0.5 with a stated power calculation, and report raw tau as primary with corrected tau as secondary, since the correction inherits the instability of a 2-seed reliability estimate. (3) Add a gating positive control: if the endpoint range between the best and worst configuration is not several times the MDE, declare the correlation analysis uninterpretable and report that instead - this is the difference between 'surrogates are invalid' and 'there is nothing to rank'. (4) Reposition the probe against arXiv:2609.02783 and add the cost-matched competitor named below; the paper's constructive claim has to be that prefix agreement beats a subsampled endpoint at equal cost, not merely that it correlates. (5) Add the per-task (within-configuration) validity analysis alongside the across-configuration one, since per-task recall-predicts-success is how practitioners actually read these metrics. (6) Budget the counterfactual labeling explicitly - injecting each candidate item singly as k=1 over 200 tasks x 2 seeds scales with pool size and is the one line item that can silently multiply the 24k-episode estimate.
reviews.missing_baseline: A cost-matched subsampled-endpoint baseline for the prefix-agreement probe. The probe is sold at 10-15% of episode cost, but the obvious competitor is to just run the real endpoint on a random 15% of tasks and rank configurations by that - a noisy but UNBIASED estimator of exactly the quantity of interest, needing no verified success trajectory and no benchmark-specific machinery. Any reviewer will demand it, and it plausibly wins, which would leave P5 with no constructive result. A truncated-rollout baseline (run n steps, score ALFWorld subgoal progress) is the second omission, and a per-task within-configuration correlation analysis is the third.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central multi-surrogate validity claim, but the check has two real holes and one unverifiable load-bearing citation. Queries I ran, all answered by the s2cli channel (S2+HF; WebSearch was unavailable in this session, so I could not open section text anywhere): (Q1, --recent) 'surrogate endpoint validity retrieval recall predicts agent task execution success memory' - returned MemOps 2607.12893, Compliance Trap 2607.10608, EvoMemBench 2605.18421, LongMemEval-V2 2605.12493, MemoryArena 2602.16313; nothing that validates a memory surrogate against execution. (Q2) 'proxy metric misleads downstream performance retrieval evaluation validity selection regret' - returned arXiv:2510.21440 (UDCG, explicitly built because recall-family metrics correlate weakly with end-to-end accuracy) and arXiv:2512.20854 ('How important is Recall for Measuring Retrieval Quality?', which measures correlation between retrieval-quality metrics and downstream response quality). Neither is in the proposal's related work, and both weaken the 'has never been measured' framing for the recall surrogate, though both are RAG-QA rather than agent experience memory. (Q3, closest named method) 'memory admission control gate precision recall downstream task success LLM agent A-MAC' - returned A-MAC 2603.04549 itself plus AttriMem 2607.21106 and 2607.06503; the proposal's reading of A-MAC as reporting gate PR without downstream validation is consistent with what I could see. (Q4, --recent) 'cheap early action prefix agreement proxy predicts full episode agent success reduce evaluation cost' - this is where the check fails: it returned EarlyEval arXiv:2609.02783 (2026-09-02, verified on S2), PACE arXiv:2607.02032 (verified), PrefixGuard arXiv:2605.06455 (verified) and arXiv:2607.06503 'Doomed from the Start' - four papers on predicting agent episode outcomes from a run prefix to cut evaluation cost, none of them cited. EarlyEval is a near-collision with P5 specifically. The proposal ran no query at all on its own constructive contribution, which is a substantive gap in the check, not a neutral. (Q5, --recent) 'LLM judge scores of stored memory items fail to predict agent execution success adversarial plausible wrong items' - returned 2608.00017 (Echo Gap, already cited) and 'Time to REFLECT' 2605.19196; no collision. (Q6) 'Prentice Freedman surrogate endpoint criterion proportion explained applied to LLM benchmark metric validity' - returned nothing relevant, which I report as empty; the formal surrogate-validity framing does appear to be unused in this literature and is the proposal's most defensible novelty claim. Verification: I confirmed on S2/HF 2603.04549, 2512.10696, 2601.03192, 2601.11969, 2608.00017, 2608.02508, 2606.23937, 2607.00725, 2603.02473, 2602.16313, 2605.12493, 2601.09503 and 2606.29914. I could NOT verify arXiv:2608.14838 'The Recall Trap' - s2cli returns 'not found on S2 or HF' and WebSearch is unavailable here, so the single closest-in-spirit result the proposal leans on (a recall-maximizing configuration lowering SWE-bench Verified resolve rate) remains unverified for me as well; the proposal is honest about this, but a claim of differentiation cannot rest on a paper neither party can confirm exists. One accuracy note: arXiv:2607.00725 is titled 'Recall Is Not Enough: A Reader-Context Diagnostic for Budget-Constrained RAG', not 'What Survives Into Context'.
